notes: Large-source-unit check: יֵרַע בְּעֵינֶיךָ → 'Let displease' is the rule 40 fusion of a contiguous predicate, preposition and noun into one English word, with the jussive frame joining under rule 17; the suffix keeps 'thee'. כָזֹה וְכָזֶה → 'one as well as another' remains noncompositional: no part of the idiom answers to one morpheme non-arbitrarily, so rule 6's first-token anchor stands.
